brief: Zero Hedge carries Goldman Sachs partner Mark Wilson's weekly note. Setup: Japanese 10yr yields are at their highest since 1996 and Gilt 30yr yields at their highest since 1998, while the VIX prints new lows for Trump's second term and MSCI World is +13% YTD, under 1% from the highs. Wilson's chain runs: Friday's payroll report makes stagflation talk hard to credit, but Waller flags next week's CPI and PPI as key. Higher global yields have been a real headwind, so apparent equity resilience masks multiple de-rating that failed to reward uniform earnings strength, and he does not resolve how much is discount rate versus an unsustainably strong earnings period. A halt to the fixed income sell-off would be unequivocally bullish for equities. Two unrelated bond drivers: geopolitical risk premia repricing oil and gas, and AI capex turning debt-funded and competing for capital. He notes focus already sits there rather than on lower oil or AI efficiency gains. Momentum reset close to 50% from late-June highs and its composition changed, so 1H leaders should not lead 2H. He would add EU defense on a 25% earnings versus price divergence, and expects rotation toward AI use-case beneficiaries.
